quote_locations.quote: All numerical notations fall into five basic typological categories, across two dimensions
of which one (multiplicative-positional) is logically excluded because multiplicative systems express power through special power signs, not through place value
it is evident that there is no perfect system
Ciphered-additive systems write numerals more compactly than any of the other types
Cumulative-positional systems use a much smaller inventory of signs than other systems
Cumulative-positional numeral systems are cross-culturally very rare, in fact, the rarest of the five types described above
such devices seem to have been developed independently in the Near East, East Asia, India, the Andes, and Mesoamerica
whereas numerical notation systems are structured through a base
tallies do not have a base
It is comparatively rare to use numerical notation directly for arithmetic even today
Numerical notations are semiotically and causally linked to, but distinct from, both the numeral words of their users' languages
twenty seventeen and two thousand seventeen are both available to English speakers upon reading the numeral 2017
the two systems dating unequivocally from the 4 th millennium BCE, are cumulative-additive
This avoids the teleological argument of Ifrah (1987) and Dehaene (1997) that sees decimal, positional numeration as the end-point of a developmental sequence towards perfection
the Babylonians only had to learn two symbols to produce their base 60 positional system

quote_verification_method: Each quote was NFKC-normalised, casefolded, every non-word run collapsed to one space, then required to appear as a contiguous word run in the BODY text of both the live capture and the Wayback capture. Caption, figcaption, script, style, noscript and template content was excluded from the body extraction. All 23 quotes are present in both copies. Paragraph numbers are the article's own printed paragraph markers, recovered by an ascending-marker scan of the retained body (1..43); the section names are the article's own section headings. Every S931 anchor's paragraph and section was re-derived after a first draft used two wrong section attributions (paragraph 3 and paragraph 1 were wrongly assigned to 'The transcoding engine'; they are in the introduction before the first section heading) and one wrong rarity attribution (paragraph 25, not 24). The corrected values are the ones in this manifest.

d_leg_shape_check.note_on_row_math: The frozen leg counts every pipe row in the section, subtracts ONE for the header, and takes the max pipe-count for columns. The staged section carries two tables (5 rows x 4 columns in 4b.1 and 6 rows x 6 columns in 4b.3), so the frozen arithmetic yields 11 rows, 10 after the single header subtraction, and 6 columns. The 4b.3 table alone is 6 rows x 6 columns (5 data rows), which independently satisfies the >=5 data rows and >=3 columns threshold if the integrator keeps only that table.
